faq.q: Why does a small brain help a woodpecker?
faq.a: The force on a brain during a sudden stop depends on its mass. A woodpecker's brain weighs only a few grams, so it can survive decelerations many times greater than a human brain could.
asks: How big is a woodpecker's brain?

faq.q: How fast does a woodpecker peck?
faq.a: Some woodpeckers peck up to about 20 times a second, and may peck thousands of times a day. Each impact lasts only around a thousandth of a second.
asks: How many times a day does a woodpecker peck?
How hard does a woodpecker hit?

faq.a: Probably not. A 2022 study of high-speed videos found woodpecker heads do not cushion impacts; they act as stiff hammers. Absorbing the shock would weaken each peck and make drilling harder.
asks: Does the hyoid bone protect woodpeckers?

faq.q: What is a woodpecker's tongue like?
faq.a: It is very long and, when pulled back, wraps around the back of the skull, held by a looping bone called the hyoid. The sticky or barbed tip spears insects deep in tunnels in the wood.
asks: Why does a woodpecker tongue wrap around its skull?

faq.q: Do woodpeckers get any brain damage?
faq.a: They seem fine, but one 2018 study found build-ups of a protein in woodpecker brains that in people is linked to injury. Scientists are still studying whether this harms the birds or is normal for them.
asks: Are woodpeckers really safe from injury?
What did scientists find in woodpecker brains?

facts: Woodpeckers can peck up to about 20 times per second.
A 2022 study in Current Biology found woodpecker heads act as stiff hammers rather than shock absorbers.
